 Medical Care Concept for UEFA club competition final matches 

1. 

Introduction 

Mission Statement 

For the UEFA final matches to be a success and to ensure the health and well-being of all UEFA Target 
Groups involved in the Finals, it is imperative that effective, expedient, and comprehensive Medical Care 
is  provided.  Access  to  medical  facilities  and  services  must  be  organized  with  minimal  difficulty  and 
bureaucracy. 

Scope 

This document describes the provision of medical Guidelines for UEFA officials, teams and VIPs at the 
final  matches  of  the  UEFA  Champions  League,  UEFA  Europa  League,  UEFA  Conference  League, 
UEFA Women’s Champion’s League and UEFA Super Cup. 

For these matches, increased medical provision is required. Firstly, at the stadium for both matchday-1 
(MD-1) and matchday (MD). Secondly, at the team and UEFA HQ hotels as well as the training grounds 
outside the MD stadium from the arrival until the departure of the UEFA Target Groups in the host city.  

The UEFA Target Group is composed as following: 

•  2x Finalists, including their teams and official’s delegation 

•  UEFA Referees, Match Officials, VIP Guests and Staff 

Responsibility and costs 

The  Medical  Guidelines serve  as  a  reference  document  for  the  implementation  of  the  UEFA  Staging 
Agreement and the Final Requirements, which stipulate the Local Organising Structure (LOS) has full 
and exclusive responsibility for all aspects of safety and security with respect to the final. 

In  cooperation  with  their  local  health  authorities,  the  LOS  has  the  responsibility  for  ensuring  that  a 
Medical  Care  Concept  fulfilling  all  requirements  set  by  UEFA  and  in  accordance  with  the  UEFA 
Requirements is provided for all identified UEFA Target Groups. 

The  LOS  is  responsible  for  the  costs  to  plan,  implement  and  deliver  the  Medical  Guidelines  for  the 
above-mentioned Final Matches. 

3 

 
 
 
 
 Medical Care Concept for UEFA club competition final matches 

2.  LOS Medical Care Concept 

UEFA will define the Medical Guidelines in this document to provide guidance to the LOS in developing 
its own Medical Care Concept. This concept will be used for the various UEFA Target Groups and all 
other relevant Target Groups as defined by the LOS. 

The Medical Care Concept must be produced in line with the UEFA Medical Guidelines and shared with 
UEFA  once  the  LOS considers  it  to  be complete.  UEFA will  then  review  the  concept  to consider and 
request potential amendments and may conduct site visit inspections before the giving final approval. 

Once the Medical Care Concept has been approved by UEFA, the LOS is then responsible to implement 
and deliver it. 

This document is designed to support the CMO in the production of the medical care concept. 

Timeline  

3.  Staffing and Resources 

This section outlines the different medical positions, which the LOS will have to appoint. 

LOS Medical Team 

The  LOS  must  nominate  a  Chief  Medical  Officer  (CMO)  who  will  be  responsible  for  planning, 
implementing and ultimately delivering the UEFA approved Medical Care Concept in the host city. 

Closer  to  the  final,  the  CMO  must  nominate  a  Stadium  Medical  Manager  (SMM)  and  a  Pitchside 
Emergency Doctor (PED) to support in delivering the medical Guidelines. 

4 

 
 
 
 
 
 Medical Care Concept for UEFA club competition final matches 

The minimum key requirements for the Medical Team are outlined below: 

•  Medical professional 

•  Experience in organising and delivering medical services at major sports events  

(e.g., international football competitions, or multi-sport events) 

•  Fluent in English 

•  Good knowledge of host city medical system and host city medical facilities 

LOS Chief Medical Officer (CMO) duties 

Duties pre-final: 

•  Primary medical contact person for UEFA in advance of the final 

•  Responsible for providing and adapting the Medical Care Concept for the UEFA Target Groups 

•  Responsible for recruitment and training of the SMM and PED 

•  Responsible to include the following information in the Medical Care Concept: 

o  The local health care system as well as insurance and payments methods, 
o  The local regulations to import medication and practice medicine in the host city, 
o  The list of Medical Facilities and organise priority treatments for all UEFA Target Groups. 

Duties during final: 

•  Primary medical contact person for UEFA during the final 

•  Coordinate and deliver Medical Care Concept in the host city 

•  Has overall responsibility for SMM and PED 

•  Keeps record of all medical interventions and reports to UEFA after the final 

•  Must be available 24/7 

LOS Stadium Medical Manager (SMM) duties 

The CMO must nominate one SMM who is responsible for all medical services at the stadium on MD-1 
and  MD.  The  SMM  is  responsible  for  knowing  the  stadium  medical  plan  and  the  local  medical 
infrastructure, which must be integrated into the Medical Care Concept. 

Please note that the roles of the CMO and the SMM can be performed by the same doctor. 

Duties during final: 

•  Responsible for delivering all medical services to be provided at the official stadium for Matchday-

1 and   Matchday 

•  Provide a clear stadium emergency and evacuation plan for any injuries/traumas on UEFA Target 

Groups 

•  Must attend the UEFA Minimum Medical Requirement (MMR) Inspections on MD-1 and MD 

5 

 
 
 Medical Care Concept for UEFA club competition final matches 

Pitchside Emergency Doctors (PED) 

The CMO must nominate one PED who is responsible for the treatment of players, team officials, the 
referee team and match officers only. The Pitchside emergency doctor is also responsible for knowing 
the stadium medical plan and the local medical infrastructure. 

Duties during final: 

•  Must be present on both MD-1 and MD 

•  Must arrive at the stadium in enough time to prepare the Pitchside medical equipment and to ensure 

all other medical services are in place and operational before the teams arrive at   the venue 

•  Must remain at the stadium until both teams have left. 

•  Must be certified and trained to provide ALS treatment as well as to recognise and manage life-

threatening conditions. 

•  Cannot perform the role of SMM for the stadium. 

UEFA Medical support team 

The UEFA Medical Unit will support the CMO in the preparation of the Finals. 

Please contact medical@uefa.ch for more information. 

4.  List of Medical facilities for all UEFA Target Groups 

The CMO must provide a list of medical facilities in the host city. 

Hospitals 

At least one top-reference hospital in the host city must be organised to provide at least the following 
services: 

•  24-hours Accident & Emergency unit / traumatology 
•  Orthopaedics 
•  Cardiology incl. interventional techniques 
•  Radiology (X-ray facilities, ultrasound (in particular soft tissues), computer tomography, magnetic 

resonance imaging) 

•  Sports medicine 
• 
Internal medicine 
•  General surgery 

General Practitioners 

At least one top-reference General Practitioner (GP) in the host city must be organised to permit short- 
notice treatment and those requiring the dispensing of medicines. 

6 

 
 
 
 
 Medical Care Concept for UEFA club competition final matches 

Dentists 

At least one top-reference emergency on-call dental services in the city must be organised to permit 
short-notice emergency treatment. 

Priority treatments 

Priority treatment must be secured in the hospital, GP and dental service collaborating with the UEFA 
Finals. The list of these facilities must be provided to UEFA 3 months prior to the final, along with the 
Medical Care Concept. 

5.  Medical services to be provided for all UEFA Target Groups 

The following medical services must be provided at the various locations listed below. 

Please note that all finalist teams are required to travel with their own (AED) and must ensure that it 
always remains in their possession throughout the duration of the Finals. 

UEFA HQ and team hotels 

All UEFA HQ and team hotels must be equipped with an automated external defibrillator (AED). 

Both teams will be provided (up on request), for the duration of their stay in the host city, with a portable 
oxygen cylinder. It will be given to the teams’ Team Medical Liaison Officer (TMLO) who   will in turn give 
it to the team doctors. Team doctors are responsible for bringing it with them to all training sessions 
away from the matchday stadium. It must be returned to the TMLOs before the teams depart. 

Training grounds (MD-2 until MD) 

A fully equipped ALS ambulance must be present and dedicated for the sole use of the players and 
team officials during all training sessions taking place from MD-2 until MD. The ambulance must be 
staffed  by  at  least  one  paramedic  and  must  contain  a  fully  equipped  emergency  bag  containing  a 
portable  oxygen  cylinder  as  well  as  an  AED  defibrillator.  It  must  be  positioned  in  an  area  that  best 
permits quick egress from the pitch area and/or dressing rooms for emergency medical evacuation and 
must be in position from 30 minutes before the training session until 30 minutes after the end. 

In case of an emergency when the ambulance is used and needs to go to the hospital, a replacement  
ambulance must arrive at the training ground in time before the other ambulance leaves. 

If teams wish to hold training sessions before MD-2, or to train at training grounds which are not official, 
MR+ can be organised at teams’ own expense. 

7 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Medical Care Concept for UEFA club competition final matches 

Stadium medical provision (MD-1 and MD) 

Emergency medical room 

The stadium must have an emergency medical room which is clean, fully equipped and ready to be used 
for all MD-1 training sessions and on MD. The room is for the sole use of the players, team officials, 
referee team and match officers. This medical room must be easily accessible from the pitch and the 
players' dressing rooms. There are no specific requirements for the minimum size of the room but it 
must be large enough to allow stretcher access and to comfortably accommodate at least one injured 
person, their doctor, the PED and must include all equipment listed in the latest version of the Medical 
Regulations in force. 

Running water and a toilet should be available in the emergency medical room. 

Provision of this facility and equipment is the responsibility of the LOS Venue Management and must 
be ready  and  available  for  inspection  when  required.  All  reasonable  requests  to  amend  the  facilities 
provided in order to meet UEFA standards must be adhered to by the LOS Venue Management. 

Ambulance service for players, team officials, referee team and match officers on MD-1 & MD  

One fully equipped ALS ambulance, staffed by at least one paramedic and a driver, must be present for 
the sole use of the players, team officials, referee team and match officers on MD-1 and MD.  

The ambulance must contain a fully equipped emergency medical bag containing a portable oxygen 
cylinder  as  well  as  an  AED  defibrillator  distinct  from  the  ones  included  in  the  Pitchside  medical 
equipment. It must be positioned in an area that best permits quick egress from the pitch area and/or 
dressing rooms in an emergency. It must be in position on MD-1 30 minutes before the first training 
session until 30 minutes after the end of the last training session, and then, on MD, 2 hours before the 
match starts until 1 hour after its end. 

In case of an emergency when the ambulance is used and needs to go to the hospital, a replacement 
ambulance must arrive at the training ground in time before the other ambulance leaves. 

The UEFA Match Delegate and UEFA Medical Officer are mandated to request that an ambulance is 
relocated if they consider that its location is in any way unsuitable in obtaining the fastest possible exit   
for an injured player, official, referee or match officer from the stadium. 

Pitchside emergency doctor 

The Pitchside emergency doctor is responsible for the treatment of players, team officials, the referee 
team and match officers only, and must be present on both MD-1 and MD. The PED must arrive at the 
stadium in enough time to prepare the pitchside medical equipment and to ensure all other medical 
services  are  in  place  and  operational  before  the  teams  arrive  at  the  venue  and  must  remain  at  the 
stadium  until  their  departures.  The  Pitchside  emergency  doctor  is  also  responsible  for  knowing  the 
stadium medical plan and the local medical infrastructure. The PED must be certified and trained to 
provide ALS treatment as well as to recognise and manage life-threatening conditions. 

Stretcher team 

For training sessions at the matchday stadium on MD-1, at least one stretcher team, composed of at 
least  two  trained  carriers  with  valid  first  aid  qualifications,  must  be  in  position  at  pitchside  from  30 

8 

 
 
 
 Medical Care Concept for UEFA club competition final matches 

minutes before the teams arrive at the stadium. On MD, two stretcher teams, each composed of two 
physically  fit,  experienced  stretcher  bearers  with  valid  first  aid  qualifications,  must  be  in   position  at 
pitchside  from  30  minutes  before  the  teams  arrive  at  the  stadium  until  their  departure.  It  is  the 
responsibility  of  the  PED  to  manage  the  activity  of  the  stretcher  teams  and  to  ensure  they  are 
appropriately positioned – in principle near the team benches and able to make eye contact with the 
4th  Official.  The  UEFA  Match  Delegate  and  UEFA  Medical  Officer  can  request  them  to  relocate  if 
necessary. 

Stretcher bearers and the PED must be clearly identified by bibs or appropriate alternative means. 

Locations and Maps of Medical services 

The locations of the ALS Ambulance, PED, stretcher teams and medical room must be identified on the 
stadium map, along with an emergency evacuation plan (see example below). 

UEFA will provide the CMO with the official stadium maps to draw and explain the evacuation plan. 

Pitchside medical equipment 

The mandatory and recommended pitchside medical equipment is listed in Annex B of the UEFA Medical 
Regulations.  We  advised  to  consult  the  most  recent  version  of  the  Regulations  currently  in  force  to 
ensure full compliance with applicable requirements. 

For  the  relevant  Finals  to  take  place,  one  AED,  one  bag  valve  mask  and  one  spinal  board  must  be 
available at pitchside on matchday and on matchday -1 where teams train at the match stadium. If any 
of these items are missing, the UEFA match delegate cannot allow the match to start. 

VIP Medical Room 

A dedicated medical room must be provided in the VIP area and must be staffed by a nurse for the 
duration that the VIP area is open. The room must contain, as a minimum, a defibrillator, oxygen and 
an equipped emergency bag with emergency drugs and airway, breathing and circulation equipment 
as specified in the pitchside medical equipment section of the UEFA Medical Regulations in force. 

9 

 
 
 
 
 Medical Care Concept for UEFA club competition final matches 

Referees 

If referees train at the stadium on MD-1 and MD, the LOS Venue Management should ensure that the 
Pitchside emergency equipment is available at pitchside and the medical room is in operation for the 
duration  of  this  training  session.  Wherever  possible,  a  trained  emergency  doctor  (preferably  the 
appointed PED) should be in attendance. 

6.  UEFA Medical inspections (MD-1 and MD) 

All UEFA final matches will be subject to inspection to ensure that the required level of medical services 
is provided. Issues/problems identified on MD-1 will immediately be addressed by the appropriate UEFA 
officials to the LOS Venue Management who will take the necessary steps to comply with the requests. 

UEFA Venue Medical Officer (VMO) 

UEFA will appoint a Venue Medical Officer (VMO) who will accompany the UEFA Match Delegate for the 
medical inspection on MD-1 as well as for the pre-match medical inspection on MD. The UEFA VMO 
will always be a qualified doctor. 

The final authority for any decision relating to an inspection (e.g. missing equipment) always remains 
that of the Delegate, although the UEFA VMO is expected to advise the Delegate on technical medical 
matters. 

Inspection schedule 

The MD-1 inspection must take place at least 60 minutes before the first team's matchday -1 training 
session at the stadium. The MD inspection must take place between 120 minutes and 90 minutes before 
kick-off on matchday. Even if no matchday -1 training session is held at the match stadium, the stadium 
medical coordinator is strongly encouraged to organise a matchday -1 inspection with the delegate to 
ensure that everything is in place for matchday.  

10 

 
 
 
 
                           
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Medical Care Concept for UEFA club competition final matches 

Both  inspections  should  be  attended  by  the  UEFA  Match  Delegate,  Stadium  Medical  Manager,  PED 
appointed for MD, the UEFA Medical Officer and, if available, the UEFA Venue Director. In addition, UEFA 
medical unit staff will attend if present. 

The inspection must include all aspects of medical service provision at the stadium including: 

•  Emergency medical room for players, team officials, referee team and match officers and its 

equipment 

•  VIP medical room and its equipment 
•  Ambulance service for players, team officials, referee team and match officers 
•  Medical staff 
•  Medical equipment including: 

o  Pitchside medical equipment 
o  Ambulance equipment 

7.  Medical information provision 

Pre-event requirements 

At least three months in advance of the match, the CMO must send the Medical Care Concept along 
with list of Medical Facilities to UEFA (medical@uefa.ch). The following items must be included in the 
concept: 

•  Local health care system 
•  National regulations on medical importation 
•  List of medical contacts 

o  CMO 
o  SMM (if different from CMO) 
o  PED 
o  Stretcher teams 

•  List of medical facilities 
o  Hospitals 
o  General Practitioners 
o  Dental service 

Please make sure to list the various services available at these facilities, their costs and the best payment 
methods: 

•  Stadium map with identified location of: 

o  ALS Ambulance 
o  Medical room 
o  Stretcher team 
o  PED 
o  Evacuation map (from pitch to ambulance and from ambulance to hospital) 

UEFA will then distribute the relevant medical information with the Match Delegate and the qualified 
finalists two weeks in advance of the final. 

11 

 
 
 
 
 
 Medical Care Concept for UEFA club competition final matches 

Matchday – team doctors 

The  UEFA  Medical  Officer  and  SMM  must  meet  the  two  team  doctors  on  arrival  at  the  stadium  (at 
pitchside). The SMM must provide each with a copy of the stadium medical plan and conduct a short 
tour of facilities with the team doctors and UEFA Medical Officer. This must include: 

Introduction to the PED and the stretcher team 

• 
•  Location of the medical room and doping control station 
•  Location of the ambulance for players, team officials, referee team and match officers 
•  Evacuation procedures in the event of serious player injury 
•  Organise the pitchside emergency briefing with the pitchside emergency doctor and both team 

doctors before the match, under the supervision of the match delegate. This meeting should take 
place 60 minutes before kick-off.
